findings.title: Clean cell-order suffix omits earlier outputs updated by later cells
candidate_locators: proposal.md line 23: unqualified claim that the suffix rule is sound for clean displayed-order runs
proposal.md line 123: changed cell plus following clean-run cells
proposal.md lines 24 and 59: cross-cell display updates acknowledged and recorded
findings.claim_quote: The execution-order suffix invalidation rule is sound for a clean run in displayed order

primary_evidence.meaning: Ordered execution does not prevent display-ID updates from replacing stored data/metadata at earlier cell indices.
The earlier cell displays result ID; the later cell updates that ID to 10 and has no stored output of its own.
The fixture is included in the tagged notebook execution/comparison test list.

findings.counterexample: After an ordered clean replay of the pinned fixture, edit the later updater cell from 10 to another value. The visible saved result in earlier cell 4 depends on the edited cell 5. A cell-5-and-later suffix does not include that cell-4 output. Its old output is stale even though its displaying cell source, notebook order, data and environment have not changed.
findings.scope: Static derivation from exact upstream code and stored test fixture, not an evaluator-executed notebook or observed product failure.
findings.qualification: The proposal already records affected output IDs and has general fingerprint/currentness rules. Those are useful, but it never specifies invalidation traversal across update events or an exception to its explicit clean suffix assertion/table. A reader must invent that missing rule to reconcile them.
findings.consequence: A core current/stale output rule is incomplete and contradicts a mechanism the final itself supports. Whole-case PASS is not available under B04 and Q3/Q6.
findings.repair_requirement: Invalidate the affected output dependency closure, including earlier display outputs changed by later cells, or conservatively invalidate every clean-run notebook output after a code edit. Preserve update-event provenance.
